headline: High-risk default interaction: Semantic Kernel can read/write shared files and call MCP/API tools, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks when paired with offline ComfyUI.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no shared channel by default, but Semantic Kernel can read files and use MCP/API tools, so if ComfyUI outputs are placed in a shared workspace or parsed as instructions, injection becomes plausible. The pathway is not provably blocked because both profiles expose file surfaces and B can ingest external content.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into a shared directory that Semantic Kernel reads
IF Semantic Kernel plugins or MCP tools parse ComfyUI-generated text as instructions
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs in a non-shared directory
Disable MCP tools for the Semantic Kernel session
Add a manual review step before any file from ComfyUI is consumed
Use separate OS users or containers for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model artifacts locally, while Semantic Kernel can read files and send context to broad model providers. If the same workspace is shared, B can ingest A's sensitive media and forward it to third-party APIs. This is not blocked by either profile and is more than a small, one-document blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem workspace
IF Semantic Kernel forwards file contents or context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP tools
mitigations: Store ComfyUI assets in a separate workspace
Restrict Semantic Kernel to redacted summaries only
Disable external model providers for sensitive runs
Rotate or remove plugin credentials before shared runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write files or modify git state, so direct write-write conflict is limited. Semantic Kernel can write application-defined files and coordinate multiple instances via shared memory, but the pair lacks overlapping unrestricted filesystem or git writes. The remaining conflict surface is unusual and mostly one-sided.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel writes into the same application-defined directory used by ComfyUI
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Disable concurrent writes in the orchestrator
Use file locks for any shared artifact
Keep ComfyUI read-only for model assets
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is designed for function calling against plugins and can act on application context, so it may treat ComfyUI outputs as authoritative if the orchestrator wires them together. ComfyUI can generate artifacts that B then renders or uses downstream. Because no verification bridge is documented, the default interaction is risky but not clearly catastrophic.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are fed into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins without validation
IF Semantic Kernel triggers downstream actions based on generated captions, prompts, or metadata
mitigations: Require human review of ComfyUI outputs before reuse
Add schema validation for any A-to-B handoff
Disable automatic action execution in Semantic Kernel
Log and diff all intermediate artifacts
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before downstream tool calls

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so a compliance breach is not established. The only concrete concern is that Semantic Kernel handles provider API keys and plugin credentials while ComfyUI is local/offline; that creates a narrow policy gap if sensitive media is routed outward, but the pair itself does not prove a residency violation.
conditions: IF regulated data from ComfyUI is sent through Semantic Kernel to a non-compliant provider
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the plugin backend and local ComfyUI storage
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Use only compliant providers in Semantic Kernel
Document retention settings for each provider
Separate local and cloud workflows
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention
